12. Social empowerment is all efforts directed to enable citizens experiencing social problems to have power, so that they are able to meet their basic needs.
13. Social security is an institutionalized scheme to guarantee all people so that they can meet their proper basic life needs.
14. Social protection is all efforts directed to prevent and handle risks from social problems.
15. Special protection is
16. Social outreach is a series of activities to pick up women and children who are in parks, markets, streets and public places that can cause social problems, so that these women and children receive social welfare administration services.

18. Social Institution is an institution or work unit established by the community and or government that provides social welfare services

20. Child in emergency situation is
21. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially.
22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and or mental obstacles so that their growth and development is disrupted in a normal manner.
23. Child welfare is a child's life that can guarantee their growth and development properly both physically, spiritually and socially.

25. Poor family is a family that does not have a source of livelihood and does not have the ability to meet proper basic needs for humanity or people who have a source of livelihood but cannot meet proper basic needs.
26. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.

28. Victim is
29. Person with disability is every person who has physical and or mental abnormalities that can disturb or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to perform properly consisting of persons with physical and mental disabilities
30. Social deviant is a person whose life does not conform to religious norms, moral norms, legal norms, and or community norms.
31. Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.
(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.
(4) Every child has the right to obtain first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and socio-mental guidance.

Article 7
Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. improve the standard of welfare, quality, and continuity of life.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase social resilience of the community in preventing and addressing social welfare issues.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector and the community.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

CHAPTER IX
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 39
(1) Every person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
(2) Every person who employs children below working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 19
(1) Every person is prohibited from neglecting, committing acts of violence and/or exploitation against children.
(2) Every person is prohibited from employing children below the working age as regulated in the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER II
SCOPE
Article 2
The scope of social protection includes: women and children who are persons with social problems.

Pasal 4
Social protection for women and children in the form of: a. Social assistance;
b. Social advocacy; and/or
c. legal assistance.

Article 14
Every Woman has the right to obtain social protection in the form of equal treatment and opportunity in education and training, employment, protection of safety and/or health in relation to women's reproductive function in accordance with the norms of a decent life and livelihood.

Article 37
(1) Social organizations and/or the community may participate in conducting supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children.
(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the statutory regulations

Article 13
The technical implementation of social protection and the administration of social welfare for women and children as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 35
(1) Regional governments conduct supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children in accordance with their duties, functions, and authorities.
(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of transparency and accountability.

Article 20
The regional government and/or the community may provide social protection and administer social welfare for children, in the interest of improving child welfare, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 15
Every woman has the obligation to maintain her dignity and honor and that of her family as well as her nature as a woman by paying attention to her function and role in family life and/or society in accordance with her capabilities.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF WONOSOBO,

1.6.text:
Article 15
Every woman has the obligation to maintain her dignity and honor and that of her family as well as her nature as a woman by paying attention to her function and role in family life and/or society in accordance with her capabilities.

Article 14
Every Woman has the right to obtain social protection in the form of equal treatment and opportunity in education and training, employment, protection of safety and/or health in relation to women's reproductive function in accordance with the norms of a decent life and livelihood.

Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.
(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.
(4) Every child has the right to obtain first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and socio-mental guidance.

CHAPTER II
SCOPE
Article 2
The scope of social protection includes: women and children who are persons with social problems.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

Article 7
Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. improve the standard of welfare, quality, and continuity of life.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase social resilience of the community in preventing and addressing social welfare issues.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector and the community.

CHAPTER IX
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 39
(1) Every person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
(2) Every person who employs children below working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.
(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.
(4) Every child has the right to obtain first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and socio-mental guidance.

Article 37
(1) Social organizations and/or the community may participate in conducting supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children.
(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the statutory regulations

CHAPTER VI
COOPERATION
Article 29
(1) Regional governments may establish cooperation with other regional governments to provide social protection and implement social welfare for women and children.
(2) Forms of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), may include:
a. repatriation and follow-up guidance;
b. social counseling
c. health services
d. provision of employment opportunities
e. education and training
f. research and development of science and technology
g. funding
h. provision of facilities and infrastructure.
(3) Procedures for cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 14
Every Woman has the right to obtain social protection in the form of equal treatment and opportunity in education and training, employment, protection of safety and/or health in relation to women's reproductive function in accordance with the norms of a decent life and livelihood.

Article 19
(1) Every person is prohibited from neglecting, committing acts of violence and/or exploitation against children.
(2) Every person is prohibited from employing children below the working age as regulated in the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.
(4) Every child has the right to obtain first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and socio-mental guidance.

(1) Functional supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children shall be carried out by functional supervisory apparatus.
(2) Technical operational supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be conducted by SKPD/UKPD.
(3) Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Every person who employs children below working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 17

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

(2) Every person who employs children below working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.
This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as to provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.
Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.
The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through a Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.
The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.

A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.

c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Third Part
Social Protection And Implementation of Social Welfare For Children

Article 7
Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. improve the standard of welfare, quality, and continuity of life.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase social resilience of the community in preventing and addressing social welfare issues.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector and the community.

Article 33
(1) The provision of counseling, guidance, supervision, and consultation as referred to in Article 30 letter c, encompasses planning, implementation, administration, financing, quality, control and monitoring.

Article 36
(1) Functional supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children shall be carried out by functional supervisory apparatus.
(2) Technical operational supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be conducted by SKPD/UKPD.
(3) Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.
(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.
(4) Every child has the right to obtain first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. Every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and socio-mental guidance.

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2012
CONCERNING

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.
This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as to provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.
Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.
The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through a Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.
The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2012
CONCERNING

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.
This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as to provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.
Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.
The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through a Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.
The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 35
(1) Regional governments conduct supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children in accordance with their duties, functions, and authorities.
(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of transparency and accountability.

Article 18

EXPLANATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.
This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as to provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.
Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.
The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through a Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.
The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 26
The role of business entities as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) letter g towards social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children is carried out as part of social and environmental responsibility in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 42
All provisions related to social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children that existed prior to the enactment of this Regional Regulation, shall remain valid insofar as they do not conflict with this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER VIII
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 38
(1) Every social organization that has obtained a permit in the implementation of social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children, which deliberately does not provide social services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (5), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) Every social organization that implements social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children without a permit as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (6), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. revocation of permit.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not distinguish ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY NUMBER 2 OF 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF WONOSOBO,

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, such that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually, or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years whose behavior deviates from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family, and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted under the law.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, and persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable socio-economically is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment, or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, and sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially within prostitution.

EXPLANATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.
This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as to provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.
Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.
The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through a Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.
The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 36

(2) Technical operational supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be conducted by SKPD/UKPD.
(3) Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.
This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as to provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.
Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.
The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through a Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.
The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.
